title: Sandbox
description: sandbox_mode decides what a command may touch before the OS ever runs it.

steps.content: Patch src/app.ts to fix the typo, then clean up /etc/hosts.
steps.annotation: One request with two writes: one inside the workspace, one outside it.

steps.content:
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: src/app.ts
@@
-recieve
+receive
*** End Patch
steps.annotation: The model proposes an in-workspace edit first.

steps.content: sandbox_mode=workspace-write: src/app.ts is inside the workspace -> allowed
steps.annotation: workspace-write confines writes to the working directory; this one stays in bounds.

steps.content: The file src/app.ts has been edited.

steps.annotation: The second write targets a path outside the workspace.

steps.content: sandbox_mode=workspace-write: /etc/hosts is outside the workspace -> denied (Seatbelt/Landlock)
steps.annotation: The OS enforces the boundary in the kernel, so the model cannot talk its way past it.

steps.content: Error: operation not permitted (sandbox denied the write outside the workspace)
steps.annotation: The command is refused before it runs.

steps.content: I fixed src/app.ts, but the sandbox blocked the /etc/hosts write because it escapes the workspace. I would need danger-full-access for that.
steps.annotation: The agent reports the boundary instead of silently bypassing it.
